questions.question: [Complex Numbers] Solve z^3 = -8. Plot the roots on an Argand diagram and show they form an equilateral triangle
questions.correctAnswer: z^3 = 8e^{ipi} -> z = 2e^{i(pi+2kpi)/3} for k=0,1,2. Roots: 2e^{ipi/3} = 1+isqrt3, 2e^{ipi} = -2, 2e^{i5pi/3} = 1-isqrt3. Distance between any two = sqrt((1-(-2))^2+(sqrt3-0)^2) = sqrt(9+3) = 2sqrt3 -- all equal, equilateral triangle
questions.explanation: z^3 = 8e^{ipi} -> z = 2e^{i(pi+2kpi)/3} for k=0,1,2. Roots: 2e^{ipi/3} = 1+isqrt3, 2e^{ipi} = -2, 2e^{i5pi/3} = 1-isqrt3. Distance between any two = sqrt((1-(-2))^2+(sqrt3-0)^2) = sqrt(9+3) = 2sqrt3 -- all equal, equilateral triangle

[Polar Coordinates] Find the area enclosed by one petal of r = 2 cos 3θ
questions.correctAnswer: r = 0 when cos 3θ = 0 -> 3θ = pi/2 -> θ = pi/6. One petal from -pi/6 to pi/6. Area = ½∫_{-pi/6}^{pi/6} (2 cos 3θ)^2 dθ = 2∫_{-pi/6}^{pi/6} cos^2 3θ dθ = ∫(1+cos 6θ) dθ = [θ + ⅙ sin 6θ]_{-pi/6}^{pi/6} = pi/3
questions.explanation: r = 0 when cos 3θ = 0 -> 3θ = pi/2 -> θ = pi/6. One petal from -pi/6 to pi/6. Area = ½∫_{-pi/6}^{pi/6} (2 cos 3θ)^2 dθ = 2∫_{-pi/6}^{pi/6} cos^2 3θ dθ = ∫(1+cos 6θ) dθ = [θ + ⅙ sin 6θ]_{-pi/6}^{pi/6} = pi/3
